title: Privacy-first telemetry and retention guardrails for embeddings + rerank endpoint
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Add a privacy-first telemetry and retention layer to the embeddings + rerank HTTP endpoints so that PII is not logged or stored by default, operators can configure retention TTLs, and audit events capture sufficient metadata for compliance without exposing user data. This ticket scopes the server-side changes, a telemetry ingestion contract, and the rollout plan across hosted and Dedicated/Private deployments.

Background: Current embeddings/rerank request and response traces sometimes contain user text and identifiers when debug logs or sampling are enabled. We must ensure production telemetry has two distinct channels: a low-fidelity, scrubbed operational stream (safe_telemetry) and a high-fidelity, policy-protected audit stream (audit_telemetry) that is only enabled for customers with explicit compliance needs and stored with stricter access controls and retention.

Non-goals: full re-architecture of vector service, UX changes in Console (separate follow-up ticket), customer self-service for audit exports (follow-up).

Constraints: Must work on Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, and Redwood Private. Dedicated/Private may need integrations with customer KMS/HSM; make config flags clear in runtime config. Changes should not add >5% p50 latency overhead at baseline traffic (bench target).
acceptance_criteria: Default logs and debug traces do not contain raw request text or embedding vectors in hosted and Dedicated by default
A new config flag 'telemetry.mode' supports values 'safe'|'audit' per-customer and per-route
Retention TTL configurable per-customer for audit_telemetry with server-side enforcement (min 7d, max 3650d)
Audit events include hashed request id (sha256) instead of raw identifiers and a structured reason code for each PII scrub action
End-to-end benchmark: enabling telemetry.mode='safe' should not increase p50 token latency by >5% vs baseline and throughput drop <3% for 128B average requests
Unit + integration tests for scrubbing logic, sampling policy, and retention enforcement exist and pass in CI
Security review approval recorded and a KMS integration test for Dedicated/Private exists
tasks: Design telemetry contract: define safe_telemetry and audit_telemetry payload schemas (fields, redaction markers, hashed IDs)
Implement server-side scrubbing middleware for embeddings and rerank routes (config-driven)
Add telemetry.mode config and per-route override logic to runtime router
Implement retention TTL enforcement job and retention metadata in audit events
Wire KMS/HSM envelope encryption hooks for audit_telemetry in Dedicated/Private
Add sampling and rate-limit rules for audit_telemetry to control storage and cost
Create unit tests and integration tests against a telemetry test harness
Benchmark performance (latency/cpu/memory) and tune batching/kernel selection to meet targets
Prepare rollout plan and canary configuration in Console (10/30/100%)
Author docs and runbook for privacy incidents and telemetry access requests

notes: Implementation should be feature-flagged. For Hosted, default telemetry.mode='safe' and audit_telemetry must be opt-in via a legal/enterprise enablement flow. For Dedicated/Private, provide runtime knobs in the 'redwood-runtime.conf' with clear defaults and a secure KMS/HSM integration guidance doc. Ensure telemetry manifests include a versioned schema to allow future changes without breaking ingestion.
